summary: Boolean gate: routes an evaluation into On True / On False signals and holds Is True / Is False as readable booleans.
description: Condition watches a single boolean input and exposes it in two forms: as level outputs (`result`/Is True and `isfalse`/Is False, plain booleans that always reflect the current state) and as event outputs (`ontrue`/On True and `onfalse`/On False, signals that fire when the condition is evaluated). Evaluation happens when the `condition` input changes, or on demand when the `eval` (Evaluate) signal is triggered — the idiomatic way to gate an action behind a check at the moment a user acts.
whenToUse: Use it to branch signal flow ('when clicked, proceed only if valid') or to derive a visible/enabled boolean and its inverse from one condition. For choosing between more than two cases use Switch or States; for combining several booleans first, feed it from And/Or or an Expression.

ports.condition: Boolean value input. Changing it re-evaluates and fires the matching signal output.
ports.eval: Signal input; re-evaluates the current `condition` on demand and fires `ontrue` or `onfalse` accordingly. Wire a user action here to use Condition as a gate.
ports.ontrue: Signal; fires on evaluation while the condition is true — not a level, it will not re-fire until evaluated again.
ports.onfalse: Signal; fires on evaluation while the condition is false.
ports.result: Boolean level mirroring the condition; wire to inputs like `visible` or `enabled`.
ports.isfalse: Boolean level, inverse of `result`; saves an Inverter when driving 'error shown' style inputs.

patterns: Button `onClick` → `eval`, with `ontrue` driving the action: gate an action behind a validity check at click time.
`isfalse` → a message's `visible`: show an error as a level rather than pulsing it with a signal.
antiPatterns: Wiring `ontrue` (signal) to a boolean input like `visible` delivers only a momentary pulse — use `result` for anything that must stay on.

Leaving Run On Value Change on when `ontrue`/`onfalse` DOES something (advance a question, navigate, set a Variable, start a Timer): the gate then fires whenever its input settles, including once while the page loads, before anyone has acted. Set `runOnChange-condition: false` and wire `eval` from the signal that should ask — a Repeat's tick, a button's click, a Timer's finish.

Two gates evaluated by one signal, where one gate's On True changes what the other one reads (advancing a question index that the other's 'is the answer right?' compares against): the second can read the changed value. Chain them instead — the reader's `done` → the writer's `eval` — so the reader decides first.
Expecting a second Evaluate with an unchanged condition to stay silent: every Evaluate fires On True or On False again, whether or not the value changed.

A gate left on Run On Value Change fires the moment its condition is true, even for one step in the middle of a chain of Set Variables. A timeout watching 'time is up AND not answered' fires again while moving on if `answered` is cleared while the countdown still reads 0: the next question starts answered and its first tap is refused (a quiz that scored the right answer after a timeout as wrong). Reset the value that makes it true (the countdown back to 10) before the one that holds it off (`answered` back to false).
